title: Dedicated Console: surface burst usage, limits, and denial breakdown for customers
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
Goal
Expose Dedicated “burst capacity” state in Redwood Console so Dedicated customers can understand: (1) whether burst is enabled for their tenant/cluster, (2) what their configured burst limits are, (3) current and historical burst usage within the billing window, and (4) why burst requests were denied (so they can debug 429s/overload and tune traffic patterns).

This ticket is the customer-facing surface area and UX glue for the feature; it depends on control plane read APIs and metering exports being available.

User story
As a Dedicated customer with burst enabled, I want to see how much burst I used (and when), what my limits are, and whether I’m being denied due to caps vs pool saturation vs cooldown, so I can plan peaks and avoid unexpected throttling.

Non-goals
- No ability to edit burst settings in Console for GA (config remains Sales/Support-admin + API driven).
- No cross-region bursting visualization (only within-region pool behavior).
- No per-request traces in Console for this first iteration (we’ll link to docs/support tooling instead).

Proposed Console IA / entry point
Dedicated > Capacity > Burst (new section)
- Summary header: “Burst status: Enabled/Disabled” and “Region/hardware class” context.
- Limits card: baseline capacity, max burst ratio, tenant burst cap, cooldown window, priority tier (if present).
- Usage card: current billing period burst usage (GPU-seconds) and/or burst tokens (if customer plan uses token-based metering); show units exactly as billed.
- Usage chart: time series of burst consumption with selectable range (24h, 7d, 30d, billing period).
- Denials card: burst admission outcomes (admitted vs denied) with top denial reason codes; include last 24h and last 7d.
- “What this means” panel: plain-language explanation + link to docs for retry guidance and common denial reasons.

Data requirements (from control plane / metering)
1) Tenant burst configuration (read-only)
- enabled (bool)
- max_burst_ratio (e.g., 1.5x baseline)
- absolute cap (if set)
- cooldown_seconds
- priority tier (gold/silver/standard), if configured
- effective policy version / updated_at timestamp

2) Usage
- burst_usage_gpu_seconds_total (billing window)
- burst_usage_gpu_seconds_timeseries (aggregated to 1m/5m buckets; keep cardinality bounded)
- optional: burst_tokens_total (only if billing is token-denominated for this customer; otherwise omit)

3) Denials / outcomes
- burst_admission_requests_total
- burst_admission_denials_total
- denial breakdown by reason code (top N reasons, aggregate remainder)

4) Freshness / propagation
- Show “Data as of <timestamp>” for usage and denial aggregates.
- If config changed recently, indicate “Config updated <x> minutes ago; may take up to <y> minutes to propagate” (motivated by prior support confusion when Console lagged config).

Denial reason codes (customer-friendly mapping)
Use the canonical reason codes from ENG-4881 / PR-23795, but display friendly labels and guidance:
- TENANT_BURST_DISABLED → “Burst not enabled”
- TENANT_CAP_REACHED → “Tenant burst cap reached” (recommend reduce concurrency / wait for window reset)
- COOLDOWN_ACTIVE → “Cooldown active” (show remaining cooldown if provided)
- POOL_SATURATED → “Burst pool at capacity” (recommend backoff + jitter; consider scheduling peaks)
- FLEET_SAFETY_CIRCUIT_OPEN → “Temporary safety limit” (link to status page / advise contacting Support)
- TELEMETRY_STALE → “Temporarily unavailable” (recommend retry; do not imply customer misconfig)

UX review checkpoints (must complete before moving to GA-ready)
- Design review with Alicia Perez: confirm layout, naming, and warning states.
- PM review with Lauren Bishop: ensure copy aligns with packaging (no promises beyond contract).
- Support/CS review with Rachel Kim + Miguel Santos: validate denial explanations and recommended next steps are consistent with support playbook.

Edge cases & error states
- Burst disabled: still show the page with “Disabled” state + an informational CTA (“Contact your account team to enable burst”) but avoid upsell-y language.
- Missing data: if usage/denials not available yet, show a non-alarming empty state (“No burst activity in selected range”) vs “Data unavailable” when APIs error.
- Partial outage: if denial breakdown endpoint fails but config loads, show config + a degraded banner for usage/denials.
- Multi-region Dedicated deployments: if customer has multiple regions/hardware classes, allow switching context (consistent with existing Dedicated capacity views).

Instrumentation (Console side)
- Track page views and export clicks for Burst page to validate adoption.
- Track “denial reason tooltip opened” to see what customers are trying to understand.

Acceptance criteria
- Customers with Dedicated + burst enabled can see burst status, limits, and usage in Console without needing Support.
- Denials panel shows admitted vs denied counts and top denial reason codes over the selected range.
- Near-limit warnings: when tenant is >80% of burst cap (configurable threshold), show warning banner and link to docs.
- Data freshness and propagation caveats are explicit (timestamped) to reduce “Console stale” tickets.
- Copy reviewed/approved by PM and Support/CS.
- No PII/tenant-secret leakage in UI; only display tenant’s own aggregates.

Links
- Design: DES-219 Burst usage UI in Console
- Control plane read APIs for Console: GitHub PR redwood/pr-23905-console-api-endpoints-for-burst-usage
- Denial reason codes: GitHub PR redwood/pr-23795-add-denial-reason-codes-and-client-surface
- Docs draft for customers: GitHub PR redwood-docs/pr-928-document-dedicated-burst-option-and-limits
- SRE dashboards (for internal cross-checking): observability-pack/pr-612-add-burst-pool-dashboards

Rollout notes
- Feature flag the Burst page by tenant (same gating as burst itself). For tenants without burst, page should be visible only if Dedicated is enabled, but show disabled state.
- During beta: default to internal tenants + beta allowlist; iterate on copy and warning thresholds based on Support feedback.

Testing
- Snapshot tests for key states: enabled/disabled, cap reached, cooldown active, pool saturated.
- Contract tests against control plane read API schemas.
- Validate aggregation rounding matches billing/export (avoid “why doesn’t Console match invoice?” issues).
comments: 2025-04-02 (Dylan Brooks): Creating to track customer-facing surfacing for burst. Needs to be GA-quality since this is where customers will self-diagnose 429s and denials. Linking DES-219 for layout and ENG-4881 for reason code definitions.
2025-04-08 (Chloe Martin): Started wiring Console backend to the new control plane read endpoints. Noted we need a clear “Data as of” timestamp; metering aggregation is batched and not real-time.

2025-04-15 (Alicia Perez): Design review: OK to proceed with the proposed IA. Request: keep “Burst” wording consistent with packaging (“Burst option”) and add an explicit disabled empty state that doesn’t look like an error.

2025-04-23 (Lauren Bishop): PM copy review: avoid implying burst is guaranteed; add note that availability depends on regional burst pool and fleet safety caps. Also ensure we don’t display raw internal pool utilization numbers to customers.

2025-05-01 (Rachel Kim): Support/CS feedback: denial reasons need “what to do next” for each. Strongly recommend adding a callout when TELEMETRY_STALE happens so customers don’t assume misconfiguration.
2025-05-08 (Chloe Martin): Implemented friendly reason mapping + tooltips. Added propagation-delay note after config updates (motivated by prior stale-config reports).
2025-05-21 (Miguel Santos): Reviewed in staging with a beta customer. Main ask: clarify units (GPU-seconds) and show billing period boundaries explicitly. No further blockers.
2025-06-04 (Chloe Martin): Shipped behind feature flag to beta allowlist. Verified usage totals match billing export within rounding tolerance. Added degraded-mode banner for partial API failure.
2025-06-12 (Dylan Brooks): Marking done for GA. Follow-ups will be separate: add export CSV and investigate per-route breakdown once label cardinality constraints are settled.
